svg.title: What stands behind a trusted landmark
svg.desc: The update service checks three things before shipping landmark subtrees. One, a reference checkpoint at least as large as the latest landmark. Two, each cosigner vouches for it: the CA and witness A cosign it directly; witness B cosigned a larger checkpoint, linked to the reference by an RFC 9162 consistency proof. Three, every landmark subtree has a subtree consistency proof against the reference. Only then do browsers get the list of trusted subtree hashes, about 10.8 KB per CA.

text.tspan: size n >= latest landmark, root R
(log, start, end, hash): ~10.8 KB per CA
the cosigners never signed the landmark subtrees. They signed checkpoints; proofs connect the two.
